related_questions.question: What is the difference between a rapid COVID test and an antigen test?

text_blocks.snippet: The terms "antigen test" and "rapid test" are often used interchangeably when referring to COVID-19 testing. Antigen tests, also known as rapid tests, are a type of diagnostic test that detects specific proteins from the virus, offering a quicker result compared to molecular tests like PCR. Both terms refer to the same type of test that provides results relatively fast.
snippet_highlighted_words: Antigen tests, also known as rapid tests, are a type of diagnostic test that detects specific proteins from the virus, offering a quicker result compared to molecular tests like PCR

list.title: Antigen Test:
list.snippet: This is a specific type of test that identifies viral proteins (antigens) to indicate the presence of the virus.

list.title: Rapid Test:
list.snippet: This is a broader term that often refers to tests, including antigen tests, that provide results quickly, typically within minutes to hours.

list.title: PCR Test:
list.snippet: In contrast to antigen tests, PCR tests (molecular tests) detect the virus's genetic material (RNA) and generally take longer to produce results.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, when people talk about "rapid tests" for COVID-19, they are often referring to antigen tests, which are known for their faster turnaround time compared to PCR tests.
